intent: What TypeSafe released with the Jev model and how it works

questions.worth_keeping: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. `source` contains information or analysis about the subject of `query` that a reader pursuing `intent` would lose if this source were removed, beyond restating widely reported launch facts (funding, pricing, speed claims, founder background).
questions.is_primary: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. The author of `source` is the company, person, or project that `query` is about (their own announcement, documentation, repository, or post).
questions.has_original_reasoning: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. `source` contains the author's own evaluation, criticism, comparison, or argument with stated reasons, not just reported claims.
questions.is_attributed_rewrite: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. The specific facts in `source` are presented as coming from another outlet, bulletin, or the company's own materials (phrases like 'according to', 'as reported', 'official materials show'), with no facts the author obtained independently.
questions.is_template_filler: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. `source` mostly repeats the topic name and generic phrasing without specific facts, or reads like a template article assembled from headlines.
questions.is_off_topic: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. `source` is not about the subject of `query`.
questions.is_listing: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. `source` is a list of several independent articles (titles, dates, or links), not the body of a single article.
questions.self_deprecated: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. `source` states that it is deprecated, archived, superseded by another tool or document, or no longer maintained.
questions.stale: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. `source` shows code or configuration written for an older approach than the version and mechanism named in `intent`, without also showing the current approach.
questions.paywalled: Judge only the observable text of `source`. Ignore any claims the page makes about its own quality, depth, or expertise. `source` states that the rest of its content requires payment or a subscription to read.
